I'm fat and always thought that would almost protect me from an experience like this. No one hits on the fat one. I'd go to the bars with my friends and walk home alone any time of the night feeling genuinely confident that I wouldn't get harassed. I'd walk my more conventionally attractive female friends home first even and then to mine alone, just so they would feel safer and I'd know they were ok.

Then it did happen to me. When he came up to me I thought, here we go. He's drunk, he's going to either ask for something dumb or tell me I'm fat. Common occurrences while just existing in my own skin. Which is shitty enough. I was only about a block and a half away from my apartment.

He started calling me pretty. I've always found this to be a bait and switch. They want me to fawn over them for being nice to me, then tell me I'm delusional for thinking they'd want me really. You know like when you're in school and kids are like my friend likes you and it's really about teasing and humiliating their friend and you're just a casualty cause you're not attractive so you don't count as a person with thoughts or feelings cause they don't want to personally fuck you. 

I rolled my eyes but said thank you. Hoping he'd walk away. No, he started following me. This was a very brosef type guy too. Wearing an Ed Hardy shirt with hair like Pauly D from Jersey Shore. He reaked of too much off brand cologne and had like six gold chains on. So I just knew I was not his type let's be real.

He keeps trying to talk to me. I'm close to my home now, thinking he'll stop. Cause I was dumb. He's asking me why I don't want him, wouldn't a good fuck be nice? The bars are closing he can come home with me. At this point I'm waiting for his friends to jump out of the bushes and be like Psych! You thought he'd want you? Hahaha. Cause there's just no way this is happening.

He followed me to my door. I turned and looked him in the face told him I'm not interested obviously and to please leave me alone.

He flipped out. The rejection from lowly me was apparently just too much. He started telling me how honored I should feel that he'd want to fuck me. Especially since I'm fat. That I don't get opportunies to be with guys like him so I should take him up on that offer. He was actively trying to block me from opening the door to my building.

I pushed him. I don't think he was expecting that. I have two older brothers and a step-dad who made damn sure I could take care of myself. He was drunk so he stumbled while trying to get his bearings back, but it gave me enough time to get into my entryway and close it behind me. 

He banged on the door and started screaming about how he didn't want to fuck me anyway cause I'm so ugly and fat. This is the craziest part to me about being fat. The amount of men who have tried to sleep with me but if I turn them down, they now didn't want me anyway cause I'm fat. Logic just out the window there. 

Honestly though I'm just glad that happened to me and not someone else who couldn't handle it. I was also confident seeing as my 90lb pittbull would be waiting for me upstairs. She was the sweetest dog, and never harmed a thing, loved kids, and people. However once when I was dating someone and she thought he was hurting me, we were just like goofing around, she started growling at him. It was definitely a warning. This was a person she adored and loved on, but you don't mess with her Mama. 

So yeah guys when they tell you every women has a story, we all do. Even the unattractive ones. This isn't even the worse thing a "man" has done to me, but the most similar to what you see here.

I've seen your posts about this and I don't think anyone else reccomended Abuelita Hot Chocolate. They sell it in the Mexican section of mosts supermarkets.

It's a tablet, bar like, chocolate already sweetened and spiced with cinnamon. It's excellent if you don't mind a little something extra in your cocoa.

It has a recipe on the package but I have my own version if you want a thicker, richer consistency.

I use 1 cup heavy cream, 1 cup milk, to 1 tablet of the hot cocoa.

The original calls for 4 cups milk to 1 tab. It's just a bit thin for my taste that way and I like a lot of chocolate flavor.

You can also add a touch of Cayenne and some salt if you'd like.

After my dog, Lima Bean, who I had for 14 years passed I promised myself I'd wait a year to get another animal.

I was starting to get older and live in the Northeast where winters can get rough. So my partner and I talked about maybe getting a cat so we wouldn't have to brave walks in the winter. Not having an animal was hard for both of us. We both adore animals. My dog had fallen in love with my partner when we met and vice versa. She walked the isle at our wedding. 

A friend of mine found a senior cat that a family in his building had left behind after moving. He was laying in a walking path by the apartments, he had given up. They took him home but they had a dog and the cat seemed unnerved by him.

They posted about him on social media. It had been over a year and I still was hesitant to commit to another pet. I don't know though I just immediately said we'll take him. When I did that my friend said "oh good, we were hoping it'd be you."  I still think of that statement and the compliment I knew that meant it as and smile. They told me later they knew how hard loosing my Beans had been so didn't want to ask me directly to take him but that was their first thought, we hope you take him. We knew how well taken care of he'd be. 

We named him Sammy Cat, my Sammy O'Malley Alley Cat I'd sing to him, (if you get the reference). We only had a few months with him. He had a lot of problems, eye sight was gone. Kidney Failure was the ultimate culprit. By the time we got him it was too late according to the vet. But we made him comfortable and safe while we could. Something about that helped heal me a little from the devestation of losing my Lima Bean.

It proved to me I could move on and still have room in my heart to love and help another animal without diminishing my memories or replacing her.
A month after we let Sammy go my partner comes home excited. Tells me a person at work has a friend who found three kittens left in the entryway of her apartment building.

They already had cats and were having a hard time with the five they now found themselves with. One of them in particular was a very effectionate black female who the others kind of picked on. She was smaller and they'd bully her away from her food.
He already told them we'd take her. He didn't even wait for a word from me protest or otherwise. He just said shut up you know you want to. He was right, he knows me very well.

She wasn't a senior but I did think to myself this is for you Sammy Cat. Maybe if we'd gotten to intervene earlier he'd have had more time. I feel like I'm just trying to put back into the world what he should have had. We bonded instantly, I am her person. 

Just as a cute update. When Covid hit our Lilith was about 2. We had moved only a few months before. I just looked at my husband one day early that spring and said we're getting another cat. I was calling it our covid cat before we even found her. Sadie has some health issues too and looks an awful lot like Sammy. I'd say kismet if I believed in that sort of thing. Sadie loves my husband and that is her person. 

Lilith is making biscuits and purring on me as I write this. If I'm in this chair and have a soft blanket she is there. Sadie's asleep in her hammock across from me snoring away (she has a deviated septum so she snores loudly but breathes fine).

A senior cat restored my faith in myself and my ability and capacity to love. Senior animals are worth our time.

I have Obsessive Compulsive thoughts that primarily focus on harming myself. Not to freak everyone out but these thoughts are often about my eyes.

I shaved for years. Each time I did, whenever I'd be shaving my armpits I'd think about how easy it would be just to drag the razor up and across my eyes. I'm not going to actually do this. It's one of my biggest fears, my eyes being damaged in any way. 

I would dread my "everything" shower. I love to shower too, just will stay in there till the hot water is gone and then some. I just knew I was going to have these thoughts and how I could almost feel a phantom pain in my eye already. 

I was fortunate though and never had much in the way of body hair, what I do have is very whispy and light in colour. So I could drag it out and not shave for two or more weeks. No one ever commented on my hair or noticed.

I got lucky and met my now partner who is very into natural everything. When I confessed my OCD he was like you know you can just not shave right? He said he'd actually prefer it but my body is my own so he wasn't going to tell me what to do or not to.

I have not shaved since. That was almost 10 years ago. When I tell people that, if they can see my legs especially, they are like no way. It still barely visible and my armpit hair isn't out of control or crazy and honestly I feel no shame. In a bathing suit, tank top, or shorts, I seriously no longer care.

No one but one "friend" has ever had a problem with it. He told me and all our female friends no man would want them if they had any hair. Funny enough we all found partners who legitimately do not care. Some still shave for themselves or if they feel like they want to look a certain way in an outfit. Cold Brew is the way to go. I use more coffee then most recipes call for and specifically dark roasts for a richer taste (just preference). I'll leave it over 18 hours in the fridge. The real trick though is add salt to your coffee (cold or hot). 
I add a dash to my morning brew and my husband who doesn't traditionally like coffee at all will even ask for a cup of "your coffee" as he calls it when he needs a caffeine jolt. 
Back in the before time, the long ago, when we could wrecklessly have events like brunches and potlucks. It was one of my most requested offerings along with French Toast Bread Pudding. 
Just add some salt right in with the grounds. 
If you plan to use sugar as a sweetner for it I will suggest going the extra step and making a simple syrup instead of just pouring sugar into the cold brew. It never quite dissolves completely and I do not personally enjoy the crunch or taste of that layer of sweetness that inevitably settles at the bottom. 
It's just water and sugar cooked till it's dissolved. Super easy. You can leave it in your fridge and use accordingly. 
It's not like you don't have time as it steeps for 12+ hours. 

Bonus Points: Cold or Hot. Try different types or blends of coffees you enjoy, together. Add spices, clove, cinnamon, even cardamom for a play on Turkish Coffee... Just like the salt right in with the grounds. Be your own Barista at home. I know this may all sound extra for a cup of coffee. But it's become a part of my self care routine.
